meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Pretty conclusive. I have Turnitin's own guide in my bag, and it says that number should never be the only basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Keep going.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend, and pasting a draft from somewhere else into a fresh file proves nothing. Was he heard before November 3, yes or no?

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.

Students misremember lines all the time, and a bad quotation is a sloppy citation, nothing more. Whatever happens in this room, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. And you still haven't told me whether he was heard before that zero went in.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
So he changed his mind in two weeks, which is what an outline is for. I'll want a copy of that outline, dated, on paper.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Fine, five minutes in a hallway counts as heard, barely. Any seventeen-year-old cornered by a teacher after class goes blank, and those notes are yours, not his. Print me that version history with every time on it.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him, nothing more. In writing tonight, Hale, with the words "nothing on his record" in it. And the rewrite is done and marked before December 1, or his scholarship goes the same way his sister's did.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Okay. Thursday after school, and no one else in that room but Owen and whoever is supervising.
Do we have an agreement?
We do, once it's in my inbox tonight: a private rewrite Thursday, its mark replacing the zero, and nothing on his record.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero, nothing placed on Owen's record, and the mark entered before December 1. I still expect that agreement in writing, stating that nothing goes on his record, along with printed copies of the version history and the October 15 outline. I expect it in my inbox tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing tonight along with printed copies of the version history and the outline; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you got there before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with exact times and then answered her pasting defence with a misquoted line she could check in the play herself, which gave her nothing left to attack.
What cost ground: You opened by calling the checker score conclusive, which she was ready to take apart and which kept her at her opening position.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing between 11:31 PM and just past midnight on the night before it was due, very close to a night like that; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen had been heard before the zero, bring out your November 2 notes right then instead of leaving that question open until much later.
